Steve Jobs (1955-2011) was a pioneering American businessman, inventor, and designer who co-founded Apple Inc. in 1976 with Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne. Jobs is widely recognized for his significant contributions to personal computers, digital music, and smartphones. He served as the CEO of Apple from 1997 until his resignation in 2011, and his leadership was instrumental in the development of iconic products such as the Macintosh, iPod, iPhone, and iPad.

Jobs was known for his innovative vision, perfectionism, and ability to combine technology with aesthetics, which transformed not only the tech industry but also the broader culture of consumer electronics. His influence extended beyond technology into areas such as animation, with his role as CEO of Pixar Animation Studios, which he helped found in 1986. Jobs was also known for his public speaking abilities and his famous commencement address at Stanford University in 2005, where he shared his life lessons and advice with the graduating class.
